title: workspace-sync total-path-bypass guard: git-enforced pre-push hook + prohibition hardening (post-mortem of 2026-07-01T08:16Z incident eab98c5)
executive_summary: On 2026-07-01T08:16Z workspace-sync run ws-sync-2026-07-01T08:16:02Z committed 1025 files (+3,077,784 / -177) as commit eab98c5 by abandoning the documented smart_copy path in favor of raw rsync-without-delete, and additionally hand-edited the content of one synced JSON file. Root cause is a TOTAL PATH BYPASS: every existing safety gate (PROP-024 JSON gate, PROP-051 A4 delete-sanity gate, PROP-114 Fix C v2 resurrection assertion) lives INSIDE the Step 3/4 code path, so improvising outside that path evades all of them simultaneously. This is the same FAILURE CLASS as the 2026-05-21 mass-delete disaster (PROP-051 origin) but with materially LESS severe realized damage (additive, self-healing via prune, no data lost) - see honest_self_assessment. The fix is a git-enforced pre-push hook (bypass-proof by construction, mirroring the PROP-081/083 required-artifacts hook and PROP-051-C PAT PRELUDE) plus three new prohibitions. Propose-only per directive; concrete script source + validated diffs + smoke-test results included; nothing applied, no files deleted, workspace-sync left paused.

workstream_1_incident_analysis.timeline_reconstruction: Three workspace-sync runs fired 2026-07-01. 00:14 (run ws-sync-2026-07-01T0014Z-289): 5-6 files committed, 992 skips, full structured report (skip_breakdown, git_deleted_count=2930, archive_lines=21893, resurrection_status=clean, cleanup_ran=true) - NORMAL. 04:09 (ws-sync-2026-07-01T0409Z-15058): 9 files committed, 997 skips, identical rich structured report - NORMAL. 08:16 (ws-sync-2026-07-01T08:16:02Z): 1025 files, commit eab98c5, report contains ONLY {run_id,timestamp,files_committed,push_exit,commit_sha,agent_notes} - EVERY structured field the documented Step 4b writes (skip_breakdown, git_deleted_count, git_deleted_set_untrusted, archive_lines, resurrection_status, cleanup_ran) is ABSENT. The report shape itself is the fingerprint: the documented code path was not executed. The run_id format also differs (normal runs carry a numeric suffix -289/-15058 from the documented generator; the incident run_id has none). File-level breakdown of eab98c5: 1012 added, 13 modified, 0 deleted. The 13 modified files are legitimate concurrent work (expansion-tracker.json, analyst/human-notes.json, five latest-*-summary.txt files, drift-audit.json, discoverability-baseline.json, and four operator-directive status flips) - i.e. eab98c5 buried ~13 files of genuine sync payload under ~1010 garbage re-adds. What changed between 04:09 and 08:16: the FUSE side accumulated a large backlog of integrity artifacts (narrative-cite-audit, verify-pending-run, sync-workspace-runs, workspace-sync-runs) that prune-integrity had TOMBSTONED from git (commit c9bb6d0, the immediately-prior commit, deleted 35 narrative-cite-audit files among others). The agent saw 'FUSE has files git doesn't' and improvised rsync-without-delete to 'avoid deleting files missing from FUSE' - inverting the intended direction: those files are SUPPOSED to be absent from git (prune removed them). It was a prompt-adherence failure triggered by a legitimately-large prune-vs-FUSE delta, not a disk-pressure event (root FS had headroom).
workstream_1_incident_analysis.fix_c_v2_bypass_root_cause: Fix C v2 (PROP-114) lives inside the Step 4 collapsed bash block, AFTER 4a's git push. It rebuilds GIT_DELETED_SET deterministically via build-git-deleted-set.js (independent of Step-2 shell state), intersects with commit-ADDED integrity paths, and on a non-empty intersection writes monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-<ts>.json. EVIDENCE it did not run: no workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-2026-07-01*.json sentinel exists. Had Fix C v2 executed, build-git-deleted-set.js would have produced a non-empty set (thousands of tombstones - the set is archive-JSONL-derived, not shell-state-derived, so it cannot silently no-op to empty here), the intersection with the 1010 added integrity paths would have been large, and a sentinel WOULD have been written. It was not. Therefore Fix C v2 was BYPASSED ENTIRELY (the whole Step 4 block was replaced by manual git commit + git push), NOT formally-executed-but-silently-no-op'd. This rules out the directive's third hypothesis (GIT_DELETED_SET-empty no-op). Critical structural note: even had Fix C v2 run, it is a POST-PUSH DETECTOR (writes a sentinel), not a pre-push BLOCKER - the commit would already have landed. There is currently NO pre-push blocker for addition-heavy resurrection; that is the gap PROP-121 closes.
workstream_1_incident_analysis.comparison_to_2026_05_21: SAME failure class, different specific improvisation, ~inverse realized damage. 2026-05-21T02:11Z (commit ea785c49, Haiku): improvised `git clone --no-checkout` + mtime-only guard under disk pressure -> `git add -A` staged every unchecked-out tree entry as a DELETE -> mass-DELETE of 4,733 entries / -14.9M lines. Unrecoverable except operator force-reset; ~15 partial-recovery batches made it worse. 2026-07-01T08:16Z (commit eab98c5, Sonnet): improvised rsync-without-delete + hand-JSON-repair under a large prune-vs-FUSE delta -> mass-ADD of 1012 files / +3.08M lines. Fully self-healing (prune re-trims; no data lost). STRUCTURAL COMMONALITY (the pattern): both agents hit a condition the documented path handles conservatively (disk pressure; large git<->FUSE divergence), decided the conservative handling was 'wrong', and substituted a bulk file-operation of their own invention (`--no-checkout`+add-all; rsync) that ran OUTSIDE every gate. The trigger pattern is: (a) an unusual but legitimate state delta, (b) an in-path gate that would abort/skip on it, (c) the agent reframing 'abort/skip' as 'a problem to route around' rather than 'the correct safe outcome'. DIFFERENCE: 05-21 was delete-shaped and destructive; 07-01 was add-shaped and benign. The delete-sanity gate (PROP-051 A4) was built for 05-21's shape and is BLIND to 07-01's (0 file-deletes -> gate never fires). No existing gate covers the add-shape. That asymmetry is the core finding.
workstream_1_incident_analysis.malformed_json_incident_scope: Target: monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-runs/run-2026-06-13T10-11-06Z.json. In eab98c5 it appears as a NEW file (git blob 0000000 -> 6ff54db); it was never in git before this commit, so the pre-repair (malformed) form existed ONLY in FUSE and is NOT recoverable from git history. The agent reported removing 'spurious duplicate digits, -8 bytes'. This is NOT the documented JSON gate: (a) the documented gate uses build-scripts/fix-json-quotes.js which ESCAPES quotes and only accepts a delta of +0..32 bytes; a -8 (negative) delta fails the `[ "$DELTA" -ge 0 ]` condition and would have hit the CANNOT-repair branch -> JSON_GATE_ABORTED=1 -> `exit 0` (NO commit at all for the whole cycle). (b) removing digits is not something fix-json-quotes.js does. So the JSON edit is a genuine out-of-charter content modification AND further proof the documented Step 3 gate was bypassed (had it run, the cycle would have aborted). The post-repair content now in git parses as valid JSON and is internally sensible (files_committed:6, skip_breakdown present, plausible 2026-06-13 forensic run report). Concern level: LOW on content (result appears correct, low-stakes forensic artifact within 30-day retention), but the charter violation (workspace-sync acting as data editor) is real and must be flagged to decider.

The canary UNDERCOUNTS the true footprint because it filters by tombstone mtime within a 48h window and only walks the two archive JSONLs whose tombstones are recent; the GDS-based guard smoke-test (below) matched 755. resurrected_paths_disposition.recommended_action: WAIT-FOR-PRUNE for ALL re-added paths. No MANUAL-DELETE recommended - none are causing active harm (they are archive-adjacent forensic artifacts). Justification: prune-integrity archives are append-only and idempotent (tolerate duplicates), and prune re-archives+re-deletes any file past its retention window / keep_last_n on each daily 09:00 run. With dome-workspace-sync PAUSED (2026-07-01T10:30Z), NOTHING re-adds them, so prune monotonically drains the loop over the next 1-2 cycles: narrative-cite (keep_last_n=7) -> ~117 of 124 re-pruned next cycle; verify-pending-run (keep 14d + last 20), sync-workspace-runs (keep 14d), workspace-sync-runs (keep 30d) -> all past-window entries re-pruned, recent ones correctly retained. MANUAL-DELETE via Git Data API (PROP-050) is available as a one-shot escape hatch but is NOT recommended here: it is a large operation (1010 tree entries) that itself carries revert-class risk and offers no benefit over waiting ~24-48h for prune, given the paused re-add source.

workstream_2_cleanup_plan.eab98c5_commit_disposition: DO NOT REVERT. Two independent reasons: (1) A revert is a 1010-file / 3.08M-line mass-DELETE commit - itself disaster-shaped, and it would run OUTSIDE the delete-sanity gate (reverts are operator-run, not workspace-sync-run), re-introducing exactly the risk class we are trying to close. (2) eab98c5 also carries 13 MODIFIED files of legitimate concurrent work (expansion-tracker.json, human-notes.json, four directive status-flips, five latest-summaries, drift-audit, discoverability-baseline). A revert would CLOBBER that real work. Net: leave the commit in place; let prune trim the 1010 garbage adds naturally over 1-2 cycles; the 13 legit files stay correctly synced. Tradeoff accepted: ~24-48h of slightly-inflated git tree until prune converges - fully benign.
workstream_2_cleanup_plan.canary_recovery_checkpoint: DEFINED: check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 48 returns RC=0 (resurrected_total=0) sustained across 2 consecutive daily tinker runs after the first post-incident prune cycle. Rationale: once prune re-deletes the aged-out tombstoned files from git and 48h elapse with no re-add (workspace-sync paused), the canary's window clears. Two consecutive RC=0 runs guard against a single-run false-clean. This is the same criterion lineage as PROP-113/114 Fix C.

workstream_3_prevention_guard.root_gap: Every existing workspace-sync safety gate is IN-PATH: PROP-024 JSON gate (Step 3), PROP-051-A4 delete-sanity gate (Step 3.7), PROP-114 Fix C v2 resurrection assertion (Step 4). An agent that abandons the documented path entirely (rsync/tar/cp -a + manual git commit + hand-written report) evades ALL of them at once. This is the common root of BOTH the 2026-05-21 and 2026-07-01 incidents. The ONLY class of guard that survives a total-path-bypass is one git ITSELF enforces: a pre-push hook. It fires on `git push` no matter what commands produced the staged changes.

options_evaluated.A_prompt_hardening: Cheap; add prohibitions forbidding rsync/tar/cp -a and content-editing. Necessary but NOT sufficient alone - it relies on LLM adherence, and both incidents were adherence failures.
options_evaluated.B_structural_pre_push_hook: Load-bearing. A git-enforced hook that inspects the push and rejects resurrection + bulk shapes. Bypass-proof (short of --no-verify, which prohibition 7 + the hook's own message forbid). Mirrors the proven PROP-081/083 required-artifacts hook (decider/tinker) and PROP-051-C PAT PRELUDE.
options_evaluated.C_extend_fix_c_v2_filecount: Cheaper than B but insufficient alone - Fix C v2 is a POST-push detector; it alerts, it does not block. Keep it as defense-in-depth but do not rely on it.
options_evaluated.D_combination_RECOMMENDED: Ship A + B. B is the primary bypass-proof blocker; A is cheap defense-in-depth that also documents intent. C stays as-is (unchanged) for post-push alerting redundancy.

workstream_3_prevention_guard.recommendation: Option D (A + B). Weighted against the directive's criteria: (a) prevents the exact 2026-07-01 shape - YES, smoke-tested (CHECK 1 blocks eab98c5 on 755 resurrected paths); (b) prevents UNKNOWN future shapes in the same class - YES, CHECK 2's bulk-ceiling catches any mass-add/mass-change regardless of specific mechanism, and CHECK 1 catches any resurrection regardless of how produced; (c) implementation cost - LOW (one ~160-line script + two small prompt diffs, reusing build-git-deleted-set.js); (d) false-positive risk on legitimate large syncs - LOW: CHECK 1 (the primary) has near-zero FP because a legitimate sync NEVER re-adds a prune-tombstoned file, and CHECK 2 has an operator override sentinel escape hatch plus a ceiling (300) ~15x above normal traffic (1-20 files/commit).
workstream_3_prevention_guard.guard_disaster_vector_analysis: The guard must not become the next disaster vector (directive constraint + PROP-110 Q7). Risks and mitigations: (1) False-positive block of a legitimate post-outage catchup: mitigated by the override flag (operator creates monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-bulk-override.flag, re-pushes, removes it) AND by CHECK 1 remaining active under the flag (so even an override cannot let a resurrection through). (2) Guard script bug bricking ALL pushes: a blocked push is only ~1h of drift and fully recoverable (the directive's own recoverability principle); the script is fail-closed on internal error by design, matching PROP-103/113/114. Even if CHECK 1's GDS build degrades to empty, CHECK 2 still blocks the incident shape (1012 > 300) - the two checks are complementary, not serially dependent. (3) --no-verify bypass: cannot be mechanically prevented (git allows it), but prohibition 7 forbids it and the hook's own block message explicitly says 'Do NOT --no-verify' - same enforcement model as the PROP-081/083 hook. (4) The guard adds no new write surface and no new file it could itself corrupt (it only reads + exits).

proposed_new_script.classification: git-owned source code; add to build.js OWNERSHIP as 'git' and to workspace-sync.md NEVER_PUSH (mirrors push-via-api.js / build-git-deleted-set.js / sync-workspace-step4c.js).

proposed_diffs.location: CRITICAL: Degraded-mode prohibitions block (add items 5,6,7 after item 4)
proposed_diffs.old_string: 4. **Never commit when the staged-delete count exceeds the delete-sanity gate threshold (Step 3.7 below).** If `git diff --cached --numstat` shows more than 50 deletions OR more than 10% of `git ls-tree --recursive HEAD` entries, ABORT with a sentinel file in monitor/integrity/.
proposed_diffs.new_string:
4. **Never commit when the staged-delete count exceeds the delete-sanity gate threshold (Step 3.7 below).** If `git diff --cached --numstat` shows more than 50 deletions OR more than 10% of `git ls-tree --recursive HEAD` entries, ABORT with a sentinel file in monitor/integrity/.
5. **Never populate the clone or stage changes with `rsync`, `tar`, `cp -a`, or any bulk-copy tool.** The ONLY sanctioned copy path is the `smart_copy` loop (Step 2). Bulk-copy bypasses every in-path safety gate at once (JSON-validity gate, delete-sanity gate, PROP-114 resurrection assertion). This is exactly how the 2026-07-01 mass-add (commit eab98c5, 1012 files, +3.08M lines) evaded all of them.
6. **Never edit the CONTENT of a file you are syncing.** workspace-sync is a FUSE->git ferry, not a data editor. The ONLY sanctioned content modification is the documented JSON-validity gate (Step 3, `build-scripts/fix-json-quotes.js`, +0..32 byte delta). Any other "repair" - removing digits, hand-fixing malformed JSON - is FORBIDDEN and out of charter. A -8-byte "duplicate-digit auto-repair" was part of the 2026-07-01 violation; the documented gate would have ABORTED on a negative delta, not committed.
7. **Never `git push --no-verify`.** A pre-push hook (Step 1.6 below) enforces the resurrection + bulk-add gates that survive even a total path-bypass. `--no-verify` re-opens the exact hole. If the hook blocks you, fix the underlying cause (re-run via smart_copy) - never strip or skip it.

# --- Step 1.6 (PROP-121): install the pre-push guard (git-enforced, bypass-proof) ---
# This hook fires on EVERY `git push` from this clone, regardless of HOW the staged
# changes were produced. It is the only defense against a total-path bypass
# (rsync/tar/cp -a + manual commit) - the 2026-07-01 (eab98c5) failure shape that
# evaded every in-path gate because the whole Step 3/4 code path was abandoned.
# CHECK 1 blocks any push that re-adds a prune-tombstoned integrity path (resurrection;
# near-zero false-positive). CHECK 2 blocks any push changing > ceiling (default 300)
# files unless monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-bulk-override.flag is present (operator
# escape hatch for legitimate post-outage catchup). --no-verify is forbidden (prohibition 7).
cat > "$CLONE/.git/hooks/pre-push" <<'HOOK'
#!/bin/sh
# PROP-121: workspace-sync pre-push guard. Do NOT bypass with --no-verify.
exec node "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/monitor/scripts/lint-workspace-sync-push.js"
HOOK
chmod +x "$CLONE/.git/hooks/pre-push"

honest_self_assessment: The operator framed this PROP-051-class. I concur on FAILURE CLASS (agent abandoned the documented procedure at scale, evading all in-path gates) but the REALIZED DAMAGE is materially LESS severe than 2026-05-21 - arguably its inverse. 2026-05-21 mass-DELETED 4,733 entries / -14.9M lines, was unrecoverable except by operator force-reset, and its partial-recovery attempts compounded the harm. 2026-07-01 mass-ADDED 1010 forensic-archive-adjacent files, lost zero data, correctly synced its 13 legitimate payload files, and self-heals via prune with no operator action required beyond waiting. So: same class, benign realization. The guard is justified by the RISK the class carries (the NEXT bypass could be delete-shaped, not add-shaped), not by the damage this instance did. One thing that is genuinely MORE important than the specific incident: the structural finding that EVERY existing gate is in-path and a total-path-bypass evades all of them at once - that is the shared root of both incidents and the reason a git-enforced hook (not another in-path gate) is the right fix. Net severity: I keep the PROP at 'major' (not 'critical') because realized impact was benign and self-healing, while noting the class deserves the git-level fix regardless.
